8.1 I have heard and considered the rival contentions of both the parties and perused the material on record.

The issue wise findings are as under:-
Issue no.(iii) Whether there is no cause of action in favour of plaintiff to file the present suit against the defendant no.1?OPD1. 9.1
Onus to
prove this issue lies on defendant no.1

. 9.2 In the written statement, defendant took preliminary objection that no cause of action has ever arisen against him, therefore, the suit is liable to be rejected under Order VII Rule 11 of The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (in short 'CPC').
The defendant has not specified as to how, there is no cause of action for filing the present suit against him.
9.3 In civil law, a "cause of action" refers to a set of facts that give rise to a legal claim.
It is the foundation upon which a law suit is built.
A cause of action or right of action, in law, is a set of facts sufficient to justify suing to obtain money or property, or to justify the enforcement of a legal right against another party.
9.4 I have gone through the averments made in the plaint and the documents filed along with it.
In the plaint, plaintiff has disclosed necessary facts entitling it for seeking recovery of money as prayed in the plaint.

As per averments of the plaint,
based upon the representations of defendant no.1, Raj plaintiff placed three purchase orders for supply of nine press Kumar machines.

The total value of the purchase orders was USD Tripathi Digitally signed 3,57,618, which was stated in the proforma invoice sent by by Raj Kumar Tripathi Date: 2025.02.07 CS (COMM.) No. 1221/2018 13:25:50 +0530 defendant no.1.
On the instructions of defendant no.1, plaintiff made advance payment of 20% of the purchase orders in three tranches.

Thus, plaintiff claims to have remitted an amount of Rs.47,43,963.30 in the bank account of defendant no.2 as advance, the details of which were provided by defendant no.1 vide e-mail dated 11.08.2015.
Thereafter, the defendants neither supplied the machinery nor refunded the amount.
Hence, plaintiff has filed the present suit for seeking recovery of its dues against the defendants along with losses suffered by it.
9.5 In view of above, this court is of the view that defendant no.1 has failed to discharge the onus to prove the issue.

Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of plaintiff and against defendant no.1.
Issue no.(iv) Whether the suit is liable to be dismissed on account of non- joinder of necessary parties?OPD1.
10.1

10.2 Defendant no.1, in para no.2 of the preliminary objections, stated that the present suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary party as the beneficiary in whose name the money was allegedly transferred has not been impleaded as a party in Skh Sheet Metals Components Pvt Ltd vs Sunil Manga on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17861876/

sentences.text: As per defendant, the said beneficiary is a proper party to the present proceedings.

He further contended that the suit is also bad for mis-joinder of proper and necessary parties to the suit due to non-impleadment of Yes Bank i.e. plaintiff's banker, who allegedly transferred the money, the banker, who partly Raj returned the money to plaintiff on plaintiff's complaint, the Kumar Tripathi party/beneficiaries in whose account the amount was credited by 13:25:57 +0530 CS (COMM.) No.
1221/2018 plaintiff's banker and the IO, who conducted the investigation upon the complaint of plaintiff.
He further contended that since the aforesaid persons/entities have not been impleaded as a party in the case, therefore, the suit of plaintiff is bad in law.
10.3 It is trite law that a proper party is someone, who may be affected by a court decision but their presence is not absolutely necessary for the court to make ruling.
The proper parties can be added to a law suit, if needed but the case can still move forward even without them.
10.4 A necessary party is someone, who must be involved in a law suit to make a fair and just decision and without them, the court cannot really resolve the issue properly.
Necessary parties are essential for the court to have all the relevant information and to ensure that the final decision is binding on everyone involved.
10.5 Mis-joinder of parties happens when someone, who is not a necessary or proper party is included in a law suit.
Mis- joinder of parties is usually not enough to completely throwout a case.
The courts often have the power to simply remove the improperly joined party and continue with the case.

10.6 In the case in hand, after going through the case set out by plaintiff in the plaint, this court is of the view that the persons, bankers or individuals as pointed out by defendant in the written statement are neither necessary nor proper parties to the present proceedings.

Their presence is neither necessary for Raj effective adjudication of real controversy in dispute between the Kumar parties nor their presence is necessary for continuation of the suit Tripathi itself.
This court does not find mis-joinder of parties in this case.

Plaintiff has rightly impleaded defendant no.1, on whose instance, the money was transferred in the bank account of defendant no.2.
10.7
In view of foregoing reasons and discussions, in the considered view of this court, defendant no.1 has miserably failed to discharge the onus to prove this issue.
Accordingly, issue no.(iv) is decided against defendant no.1 and in plaintiff's favour.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
. 9.2 In the written statement, defendant took preliminary objection that no cause of action has ever arisen against him, therefore, the suit is liable to be rejected under Order VII Rule 11 of The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (in short 'CPC').
The defendant has not specified as to how, there is no cause of action for filing the present suit against him.
9.3 In civil law, a "cause of action" refers to a set of facts that give rise to a legal claim.
It is the foundation upon which a law suit is built.
A cause of action or right of action, in law, is a set of facts sufficient to justify suing to obtain money or property, or to justify the enforcement of a legal right against another party.
Thereafter, the defendants neither supplied the machinery nor refunded the amount.
Hence, plaintiff has filed the present suit for seeking recovery of its dues against the defendants along with losses suffered by it.
10.3 It is trite law that a proper party is someone, who may be affected by a court decision but their presence is not absolutely necessary for the court to make ruling.
The proper parties can be added to a law suit, if needed but the case can still move forward even without them.
10.4 A necessary party is someone, who must be involved in a law suit to make a fair and just decision and without them, the court cannot really resolve the issue properly.
Necessary parties are essential for the court to have all the relevant information and to ensure that the final decision is binding on everyone involved.
10.5 Mis-joinder of parties happens when someone, who is not a necessary or proper party is included in a law suit.
Mis- joinder of parties is usually not enough to completely throwout a case.
The courts often have the power to simply remove the improperly joined party and continue with the case.
10.6 In the case in hand, after going through the case set out by plaintiff in the plaint, this court is of the view that the persons, bankers or individuals as pointed out by defendant in the written statement are neither necessary nor proper parties to the present proceedings.
Their presence is neither necessary for Raj effective adjudication of real controversy in dispute between the Kumar parties nor their presence is necessary for continuation of the suit Tripathi itself.
This court does not find mis-joinder of parties in this case.
The defendant has not specified, who was the legally competent person on behalf of plaintiff, to file the present suit.
Mr. Abhinay Singh has filed the instant suit for recovery against defendants.
Thus, in the absence of anything contrary on record, Raj this court holds that the instant suit has been filed by plaintiff Kumar through a legally authorized and competent person on behalf of Tripathi Digitally signed plaintiff.
The defendant has not specified as to how the suit of plaintiff is barred by limitation and for how much time.
Thus, the plea of defendant that the suit of plaintiff is barred by limitation is found to be without any basis and substance.
Thus, the suit of plaintiff is found to be well within limitation.
The bank account details of defendant no.2 in which plaintiff transferred the money were provided via e-mail by defendant no.1.
The defendants despite payment being made by plaintiff have neither supplied the machinery nor refunded the advance amount paid by it.
14.18 Defendant no.1 has neither examined himself nor produced any other witness to prove the averments made in the written statement.
Thus, the defence as taken in the written statement could not be proved on record.
Defendant has failed to Tripathi prove on record that he ever made any complaint to police regarding hacking of his mail at any point of time.
He has also not provided the details as to when his mail was hacked and when he came to know about such hacking, if any.
The defendant has always communicated with plaintiff on the same e- mail ID i.e. presstek@gmail.com.
before and after the alleged transaction.
Thus, in the absence of any cogent and credible evidence on record, the defence of hacking of his e-mail account, taken by defendant no.1 cannot be believed.
14.21 Defendant no.1 has further contended that plaintiff also got registered FIR No.13/2016 u/s 420 IPC in respect of the alleged transaction in dispute.
Investigation in the said FIR was conducted by the police but the police failed to find out the actual offender.
Therefore, the Investigating Officer has already filed untrace report in the court of competent jurisdiction.
It is well settled that a party can seek civil as well as criminal remedy simultaneously.
It is equally well settled that findings of a criminal court are not binding on civil court.
The standard of proof in civil cases as well as criminal cases are also different.
A civil case is decided on the principle of preponderance of probability while, in criminal case, prosecution has to prove its case against accused beyond all shadow of reasonable doubt.
